title: Operator cancels active rent within grace period without penalty
gherkin:
Feature: Operator Grace-Period Cancellation
  Scenario: Operator cancels active rent within grace period
    Given an active rent record in 'Active' status
    And the rent was created less than the grace period duration ago
    And the operator has OPERATOR role
    When the operator initiates a cancellation request
    Then the cancellation is processed successfully
    And no penalty fee is applied
    And the rent status changes to 'Cancelled'
rationale: Core requirement: operators must be able to cancel active rents within the grace period without incurring penalties. This test validates the primary feature of R30.
usedContextItems: Operator grace-period cancellation is a feature that allows authorized users (OPERATOR or ADMIN roles) to cancel active rents within a defined tolerance window without triggering penalty fees|The system must distinguish between cancellations within the grace period (no penalty) and cancellations after the grace period (penalty applies)

Date: 2026-02-20 14:00
Subject: URGENT: Special Maintenance Rule for Concrete Mixers

Hi Team,

Regardless of what the current SRS (v1.2) says about the dynamic Maintenance Matrix, we have an emergency with Concrete Mixers. 120 minutes is absolutely not enough for proper cleaning/maintenance.

Effective immediately:
- Concrete Mixers MUST have a 12-hour (720 min) maintenance window.
- All other machinery can stay at the 2-hour (120 min) rule for now.

Please hardcode this for the Mixer category until the official Matrix is published in the next SRS version.

Best regards,
Tom (Operations Lead)

From: finance_director@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-03-03 11:00
Subject: Pilot concern about international billing presentation

Hi Team,

Finance has a concern related to the pilot rollout for internationally billed equipment.

For a subset of high-value inventory, we may need a billing presentation approach that works more cleanly across more than one currency context. The current specification covers general pricing and billing expectations, but it does not go into much detail about how pilot-specific currency presentation or conversion rules should be handled in customer-facing outputs.

Before any implementation shortcut is taken, please clarify whether currency conversion, display format, and invoice currency are supposed to be handled as strict accounting rules, temporary pilot behavior, or only a presentation-layer convention. We want to avoid a situation where the operational display becomes simpler, but the customer-visible totals no longer align cleanly with the underlying financial records.

Best,
Finance Dept.

Subject: Registration consent flow must be revised before launch

Hi All,

During the latest compliance review, Legal raised a blocking concern regarding how consent is collected in the registration journey.

At the moment, the current approach appears to bundle multiple legal acknowledgements too closely. For launch readiness, users need to express consent to the contractual terms and the personal-data-related notice in a clearly distinguishable way. A single combined acknowledgement is not sufficient for this purpose.

Please adjust the registration flow so that these approvals are captured independently and can be demonstrated separately if needed during audit.

This is a release-blocking compliance item.

Best regards,

Dr. Arpad Jog
General Counsel

Hi Team,

Finance has a concern related to the pilot rollout for internationally billed equipment.

Best,
Finance Dept.
